summary: The paper classifies Fortran D compiler optimizations for MIMD distributed-memory machines by the cost they reduce: startup, copy and transit time, or lack of parallelism. It evaluates them on Livermore, Jacobi, SOR and ADI kernels on an Intel iPSC/860 and derives profitability formulas for each.
why_read: It shows with measurements which communication and parallelism optimizations matter most for a data-parallel compiler, and where they stop paying off.
main_contribution: A classification of Fortran D optimizations, cost formulas for them, and an empirical comparison of their effects on iPSC/860 kernels.
main_limitation: Results come from one machine and a small set of kernels, several optimizations were applied by hand, and the cost model keeps communication cost fixed per message.
evaluation_method: Timings of hand-selected kernel versions on 8 to 32 nodes of an Intel iPSC/860, compared with a no-communication baseline and with analytic cost formulas.
